questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was ok, but housing from the school (both off and on campus) was only available to non-eu citizens.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Apply for the courses and collect your student ID – it is all explained in the mails from Queen Mary you will recieve.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Whatever was needed – both on campus in person and over email if necessary.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I got the courses I had hoped, but the academic level could've been higher.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was a 'BaKa' student at UCPH so I took both BA and MA classes. The academic level at Queen Mary did not seem to be quite as high as at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was exactly the same – but quizzes / presentations during the semester counts towards your final grade (so not only just one final exam that counts for 100% like at UCPH).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Games & Strategies
Health Economics
Environmental Economics
History of Economic Thought

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Games & Strategies – by far the most interesting course I took and reminds a lot of "Microeconomics III" at UCPH.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was a part of the Golf Society at Queen Mary – 10/10 would recommend even if you haven't played golf. The social arrangements and teaching of golf was top top top.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was basically a club for everything you can imagine.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, culture is a lot like the danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Take part in the clubs events and don't say no to the pub after school (english people love the pub).

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Do well during the semester for significantly less stress during the exams.
Take part in whatever clubs interest you the most at the school.
Make friends in your different classes.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *

What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Nothing really challenging to be honest.
